question.:question/problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/generate/scratch/17592186133930/plots/9650b1f1e873aa9cfaaf.png)

Consider the vector field $F=⟨2\left(1-2x\right),\,2\left(5y-3{z}^{2}\right),\,2\left({x}^{3}-{y}^{2}\right)⟩$ and the surface $S$ defined by the bounding region of a right circular cylinder of height $2$ whose base is a circle of radius $3$ centered at the origin, as shown above. Given that $S$ is positively (outward) oriented, use the divergence theorem to find the flux of $F$ through $S.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $R$ be a simple solid region bounded by a closed surface $S$ with positive (outward) orientation. If a vector field $F$ has continuous partial derivatives for all its components in an open region in space that contains $R,$ then the divergence theorem states that

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS={∭}_{R}\text{div}\,F\,\text{d}V.
$$

Computing the divergence of $F,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{div}\,F & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(2\left(1-2x\right))+\frac{∂}{∂y}(2\left(5y-3{z}^{2}\right))+\frac{∂}{∂z}(2\left({x}^{3}-{y}^{2}\right)) \\  & =(-4)+10+0 \\  & =6.\end{aligned}
$$

Let $R$ be the solid cylinder enclosed by $S.$ Then, using the divergence theorem, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS & ={∭}_{R}6\,\text{d}V \\  & =6{∭}_{R}\,\text{d}V \\  & =6\cdot \text{Volume}(R) \\  & =6\cdot \pi \cdot {3}^{2}\cdot 2 \\  & =108 \pi.\end{aligned}
$$

Let $R$ be a simple solid region bounded by a closed surface $S$ with positive (outward) orientation. If a vector field $F$ has continuous partial derivatives for all its components in an open region in space that contains $R,$ then the divergence theorem states that

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS={∭}_{R}\text{div}\,F\,\text{d}V.
$$

Computing the divergence of $F,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{div}\,F & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({y}^{2}-2{x}^{2}+6xy)+\frac{∂}{∂y}(2y-3{y}^{2})+\frac{∂}{∂z}(4xz) \\  & =-4x+6y+(2-6y)+4x \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Let $R$ be the solid sphere of radius $3$ enclosed by $S.$ Then, using the divergence theorem, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS & ={∭}_{R}2\,\text{d}V \\  & =2{∭}_{R}\,\text{d}V \\  & =2\cdot \text{Volume}(R) \\  & =2\cdot \frac{4}{3}\pi \cdot {3}^{3} \\  & =72 \pi.\end{aligned}
$$
